newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares balloon as foreign appetite grows.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares balloon as foreign appetite grows.

text.p: Slovenian shares on Friday added on to this year's heady gains, jumping more than four percent on what traders said appeared to be insatiable foreign demand.
Traders said they were confident the bull run would continue over the medium term as foreign buying has triggered catch-up buying from domestic investors.
The 10-share SBI index surged 64.07 points or 4.53 percent to 1,479.4. The blue-chip index has now risen 15.8 percent after six consecutive days of gains.
"This is a madhouse -- all shares are going up and...it seems like foreign investors still feel prices are low," said Goran Brankovic, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska banka.

"It seems foreigners have definitely decided to come to our market after it became clear that the Bank of Slovenia will not prevent foreign buying and that all political parties support membership of the European Union," said Toni Apollonio, an analyst at bank A banka.
Food company Kolinska was the most actively traded share, jumping 6.96 percent to 2,460 tolars on volume of 80,387 shares for total turnover of 194.4 million tolars.
Market turnover surged to 591.7 million tolars from 459.2 million. Overall 15 shares rose, two fell, one was unchanged, and seven were untraded.
Traders also attributed the market's bull run to hopes for significant increases in profits from certain blue-chip firms.
"Flotation of some local companies abroad is approaching and that is also pushing prices higher," one trader said.
The Bank of Slovenia this week approved Slovenia's second largest bank SKB to list its shares in London. SKB is likely to be the first Slovenian company to do so.
The preferred shares of trader Kovinotehna were the biggest gainers, jumping 10.4 percent to 552 tolars on volume of 6,598 shares, for total turnover of 3.6 million tolars.
Financial consultancy Primofin led the day's decliners, falling 4.42 percent to 17,510 tolars on volume of 181 shares for total turnover of 3.3 million.
